mainTopic: פשרה in judgment, אהרן and the עגל, folk sayings matched to פסוקים, and the serious responsibility of a דיין
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of פשרה. רבי יהושע בן קרחה holds it is a מצוה to offer the sides a choice between דין and פשרה. The תנא קמא holds it is only רשות. רבי שמעון בן מנסיא forbids suggesting פשרה once the judge knows which way the ruling leans. Next, רבי תנחום בר חנילאי reads the פסוק about the 'בוצע' as speaking of אהרן. אהרן saw חור killed, so he let the people make the עגל, a sin that can be fixed through תשובה. The other תנאים read 'פוטר מים ראשית מדון' like רב המנונא, and רב הונא and אביי קשישא add pictures showing that a quarrel must be stopped early. A series of folk sayings follows, each matched with a פסוק by שמואל or רב הונא. The גמרא then proves from three פסוקים that 'לא תגורו' can mean 'gathering in'. Finally, רבי שמואל בר נחמני in the name of רבי יונתן gives three teachings about the great responsibility of a judge, and the last one continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What the מצוה of compromise means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יהושע בן קרחה's 'מצוה' is to offer the sides a choice: strict דין or פשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a מצוה to say to them: Do you want strict judgment, or do you want a compromise?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining what רבי יהושע בן קרחה meant when he called פשרה a 'מצוה'. The judge must offer the two sides a choice between strict law and compromise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן קרחה does not mean the judge must force a פשרה on the sides. The מצוה is only to put the choice in front of them. This keeps room for strict דין if the sides want it.

keyTerms.meaning: A commandment; something one is obligated or encouraged to do
Strict judgment according to the letter of the law
A compromise between the two sides

phrases.english: It is a מצוה to say to them:
phrases.notes: This explains what רבי יהושע בן קרחה meant earlier when he called compromise a מצוה.

phrases.english: Do you want strict judgment,
or do you want a compromise?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the meaning of רבי יהושע בן קרחה's statement from the previous section of the daf.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly is the 'מצוה' of פשרה according to רבי יהושע בן קרחה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The judge must offer the sides a choice between דין and פשרה.

steps.title: Isn't this the same as the תנא קמא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges that רבי יהושע בן קרחה seems to say nothing new, since the תנא קמא also allows פשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the same as the תנא קמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that רבי יהושע בן קרחה's view looks the same as the תנא קמא's, who also allows compromise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both opinions allow פשרה, there is no reason to record רבי יהושע בן קרחה as a separate opinion. The גמרא wants to find a real difference between them.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the same as (a challenge that two views do not differ)
The first, unnamed opinion in the ברייתא

phrases.english: This is the same as the first tanna!
phrases.notes: The first תנא said compromise is allowed until the verdict is finished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation in step 1 because it seems to make the opinion redundant.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion of רבי יהושע בן קרחה as explained in step 1
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two opinions that say the same thing should not be listed separately.

steps.title: The difference: מצוה or only permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן קרחה holds offering פשרה is a מצוה. The תנא קמא holds it is only רשות (permitted).
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them about מצוה: רבי יהושע בן קרחה holds it is a מצוה, and the תנא קמא holds it is merely permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two opinions differ in degree. One says offering פשרה is a מצוה, and the other says it is only allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that פשרה is allowed. The new point is how strongly. For רבי יהושע בן קרחה the judge should actively offer it. For the תנא קמא the judge may offer it but does not have to.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

phrases.english: There is a difference between them: מצוה.
phrases.notes: In other words, they argue about whether offering compromise is a מצוה.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה סָבַר מִצְוָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha holds it is a מצוה,
the first tanna holds it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the strength of the ruling (מצוה versus רשות)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two opinions seemed the same because both allow פשרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ: מצוה for רבי יהושע בן קרחה, only רשות for the תנא קמא.

steps.title: Then isn't the תנא קמא the same as רבי שמעון בן מנסיא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges that if the תנא קמא holds פשרה is only רשות, he now seems identical to רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this the same as רבי שמעון בן מנסיא?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the תנא קמא is defined as 'permitted, not a מצוה', the גמרא asks whether he says the same thing as רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא also allows פשרה without requiring it. Fixing the first problem seems to have created a new one: now the תנא קמא looks redundant.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא in the ברייתא who sets limits on when the judge may suggest פשרה

phrases.english: Is this the same as Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya?
phrases.notes: The 'this' is the first תנא's view, now understood as 'compromise is allowed but not required.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 3 to raise a new problem of redundancy.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא קמא as defined in step 3
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the תנא קמא holds 'רשות', he seems to match רבי שמעון בן מנסיא, so one of them is redundant.

steps.title: The difference: once you know where the ruling leans
steps.stepSummary: They differ about the stage after the judge hears the claims and knows which way the דין leans. רבי שמעון בן מנסיא forbids suggesting פשרה then.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: after you hear their statements and you know where the judgment is leaning, you are not permitted to say to them 'Go out and compromise.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two differ about timing. רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says that once the judge knows where the ruling is heading, he may no longer suggest a פשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line quoted here is רבי שמעון בן מנסיא's own limit. The תנא קמא allows פשרה even at that stage, all the way until the verdict is finished. So the two opinions are not the same.

keyTerms.meaning: Make a compromise (from בצע, to split or settle)

steps.confusionAlert: The rule quoted here, 'you may not say go and compromise', belongs to רבי שמעון בן מנסיא. The תנא קמא disagrees and still allows פשרה at this stage.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels. רבי יהושע בן קרחה says offering פשרה is a מצוה. The תנא קמא says it is permitted until the verdict. רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says it is permitted only until the judge knows which way the ruling leans.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them:
After you hear their statements
and you know where the judgment is leaning,

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה רַשַּׁאי לוֹמַר לָהֶן ״צְאוּ וּבִצְעוּ״.
phrases.english: you are not permitted to say to them: 'Go out and compromise.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing by stage of the case (timing)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא and רבי שמעון בן מנסיא seemed identical.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once the judge knows which way the ruling leans, רבי שמעון בן מנסיא forbids suggesting פשרה, while the תנא קמא still allows it.

steps.title: רבי תנחום reads the פסוק as being about the עגל
steps.stepSummary: The earlier readings of 'ובוצע ברך נאץ ה'' argue with רבי תנחום בר חנילאי, who says the פסוק refers to מעשה העגל and אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this argues with רבי תנחום בר חנילאי, for רבי תנחום בר חנילאי said: This פסוק was said only about the incident of the עגל, as it says: 'And אהרן saw, and he built an altar before it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section. It brings רבי תנחום בר חנילאי, who explains the פסוק about the 'בוצע' as speaking about אהרן at חטא העגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on the daf, other חכמים explained 'בוצע' in the פסוק as referring to other people. רבי תנחום says the פסוק is really about אהרן, who 'compromised' with the people at the עגל. He brings a פסוק from the story of the עגל to start his proof.

keyTerms.meaning: And this argues with (a different opinion)
The incident of the Golden Calf

phrases.english: And this argues with Rabbi Tanchum bar Chanilai,
phrases.notes: The earlier explanations of the פסוק 'ובוצע ברך נאץ ה'' (תהלים 10:3) are the ones that argue with him.

phrases.english: for Rabbi Tanchum bar Chanilai said:
This verse was not said
except about the incident of the Calf,
as it says: 'And Aaron saw
and he built an altar before it.'
phrases.notes: שמות 32:5

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the halachic discussion of פשרה to an aggadic reading of the פסוק about the 'בוצע'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק 'ובוצע ברך נאץ ה'' refers to אהרן at מעשה העגל.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the topic of 'compromise' to a famous story. It shows that compromising with wrongdoing can be seen as provoking ה'.

steps.title: What did אהרן see?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what אהרן 'saw' in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did he see?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word 'וירא' (and he saw) is referring to. It is setting up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says אהרן saw, but it does not say what he saw. The question opens the door to a reading that explains why אהרן built the altar.

phrases.english: What did he see?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in the פסוק quoted in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What did אהרן see that led him to build the altar?

steps.title: He saw חור slaughtered before him
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that אהרן saw חור killed in front of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי בנימין בר יפת said in the name of רבי אלעזר: He saw חור slaughtered before him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: אהרן saw that חור had been killed in front of him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מזבח' (altar) is read as 'זבוח' (slaughtered). So the פסוק is hinting that אהרן understood the danger from what had happened to חור. This explains why אהרן went along with the people.

keyTerms.meaning: The leader who was with אהרן while משה was on the mountain

phrases.english: Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet said
that Rabbi Elazar said:
He saw Hur, who was slaughtered before him.
phrases.notes: It's a play on words: 'מזבח לפניו' (an altar before him) is read as 'זבוח לפניו' (slaughtered before him).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי בִּנְיָמִין בַּר יֶפֶת אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אהרן saw חור slaughtered before him.

steps.title: אהרן's reasoning: better a sin that can be fixed
steps.stepSummary: אהרן reasoned that if he refused, they would kill him as well. That sin could never be fixed, while worshipping the עגל could be fixed through תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: If I don't listen to them now, they will do to me what they did to חור, and the פסוק 'Shall the priest and prophet be killed in the Sanctuary of God?' will be fulfilled through me, and they will never have a remedy. Better that they worship the עגל, since perhaps they can have a remedy through תשובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes what אהרן thought after seeing חור killed. He chose the lesser evil so the people would still have a way to do תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אהרן compared two sins. Killing a כהן and a נביא would leave the people with no remedy forever. Worshipping the עגל could still be fixed through תשובה. This is the 'compromise' that רבי תנחום says the פסוק about the 'בוצע' refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: A remedy, a way to fix the situation
A priest and a prophet (אהרן was both)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי תנחום בר חנילאי, the 'בוצע' in the פסוק is אהרן. He compromised with the people at the עגל to prevent a sin that could never be fixed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: אִי לָא שָׁמַעְנָא לְהוּ הַשְׁתָּא,
phrases.english: He said: If I do not listen to them now,
phrases.notes: 'He' is אהרן, speaking to himself.

phrases.english: they will do to me as they did to Hur,
and it will be fulfilled through me:
'Shall the priest and prophet be killed in the Sanctuary of God?'
phrases.notes: איכה 2:20

phrases.english: and they will never have a remedy.
Better that they worship the Calf,
since it is possible they will have a remedy through repentance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: אִי לָא שָׁמַעְנָא לְהוּ הַשְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues step 8 by explaining what אהרן concluded from seeing חור killed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אהרן chose to let the people worship the עגל, a sin that can be fixed by תשובה, rather than let them kill a כהן and נביא, a sin with no remedy.

steps.title: How do the other תנאים use the פסוק about strife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the תנאים who did not learn 'פוטר מים ראשית מדון' about פשרה learn from this פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these תנאים, what do they learn from the פסוק 'The beginning of strife is like letting out water'?
steps.whatsHappening: Earlier, a תנא used the פסוק 'פוטר מים ראשית מדון' to teach when a judge may suggest פשרה. Now the גמרא asks what the other תנאים, who did not read it that way, learn from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes every פסוק teaches something. If these תנאים don't use this פסוק for the laws of פשרה, they must use it for some other lesson. This question sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנאים, the sages of the משנה period
'The beginning of strife is like letting out water' (משלי 17:14)
What do they learn from it?

phrases.english: And these תנאים
phrases.notes: He means the תנאים who did not use this פסוק for the rules of פשרה.

phrases.english: "The beginning of strife is as when one releases water"
phrases.notes: משלי 17:14

phrases.english: what do they learn from it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי ״פּוֹטֵר מַיִם רֵאשִׁית מָדוֹן״, מַאי דָּרְשִׁי בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the אהרן discussion to the earlier argument about פשרה, and asks how the other side reads the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson the other תנאים take from 'פוטר מים ראשית מדון' if they don't apply it to פשרה.

steps.title: A person is first judged on Torah
steps.stepSummary: They learn it like רב המנונא: the first thing a person is judged on is דברי תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like רב המנונא, for רב המנונא said: The first thing a person is judged on is only Torah, as it says, 'The beginning of strife is like letting out water.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that these תנאים use the פסוק like רב המנונא. The first thing a person is judged on is how he learned Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'ראשית מדון' (the beginning of the case) is read as the start of a person's judgment, and 'מים' (water) stands for Torah. So the פסוק is about Heavenly judgment, not about פשרה in a בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא whose teaching is used here

phrases.english: Like the teaching of Rav Hamnuna
for Rav Hamnuna said
The beginning of a person's judgment
is judged only on matters of Torah
phrases.notes: This is about the judgment in Heaven after a person dies.

phrases.english: as it is said: "The beginning of strife is as when one releases water"
phrases.notes: Water here is a picture for Torah. The 'beginning of the case' is about Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They read the פסוק like רב המנונא: a person's judgment begins with Torah.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that both sides of the earlier argument use the same פסוק, each for a different lesson.

steps.title: A quarrel is like a crack in a water channel
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא compares a quarrel to a crack in a water channel: once it widens, it keeps widening.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: A quarrel is like a crack in a water channel. Once it widens, it keeps widening.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a picture of how a fight grows, based on the water image in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small crack lets water out, and the water rushes through and makes the crack bigger. A fight works the same way: each round makes it worse. So it must be stopped right at the start.

keyTerms.meaning: A crack in a water channel

phrases.english: Rav Huna said
This quarrel
is like a crack in a water channel
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, 'of water'. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: once it widens, it keeps widening

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: הַאי תִּיגְרָא דָּמְיָא לְצִינּוֹרָא דְּבִידְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a lesson about quarrels from the same פסוק's image of released water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A quarrel grows like a widening crack, so stop it early.

steps.title: A quarrel is like a bridge plank that sets firmly
steps.stepSummary: אביי קשישא compares a quarrel to a plank in a bridge: once it settles in place, it stays fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי קשישא said: It is like a plank of a bridge. Once it sets, it stays set.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי קשישא makes the same point as רב הונא with a different picture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plank that has settled into place becomes hard to move. A fight that has been going on for a while becomes fixed and hard to undo. Both pictures teach that the best time to end a fight is right at the beginning.

keyTerms.meaning: Once it stands firm, it stays firm

phrases.english: Abaye the Elder said
It is like a plank of a bridge
phrases.notes: 'It' is the quarrel from רב הונא's line.

phrases.english: once it has set firmly, it stays firm

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי קַשִּׁישָׁא אָמַר: דָּמֵי לְגוּדָּא דְּגַמְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel picture to רב הונא's crack in the channel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A quarrel hardens like a settled plank, so end it early.
steps.whatToRemember: Both pictures teach one lesson: stop a fight as soon as it starts, before it grows or hardens.

steps.title: A memory aid for the coming sayings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a memory aid, 'שמעי ושתי שבע זמירות הוא', for the series of sayings that comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'שמעי ושתי שבע זמירות הוא' is a memory aid.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next part. The גמרא gives a memory aid to help us remember the order of several stories about popular sayings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word in the memory aid hints at one of the coming stories. The first word, שמעי, matches the next story, about a man who hears (שמע) insults and stays silent.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid for remembering a list
The words of the memory aid, each hinting at a coming story

steps.confusionAlert: Don't try to translate this line as a sentence with a meaning. It is only a string of hint-words for remembering the stories in order.

phrases.english: Shimi ushti
sheva zemirot hu, is a memory aid

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁמְעִי וּשְׁתֵּי שֶׁבַע זְמִירוֹת הוּא, סִימָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A transition line that sets up a series of popular sayings connected to the theme of quarrels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A memory aid for the order of the stories that follow.

steps.title: A passerby praises staying silent
steps.stepSummary: A man walking along kept saying: Fortunate is the one who hears insults and stays silent, because a hundred troubles pass him by.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who kept saying as he walked: Fortunate is the one who hears and stays silent. A hundred troubles pass him by.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the first story: a common saying that a passerby was repeating. This sets up the next step, where שמואל finds this idea in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying teaches that if someone is insulted and does not answer back, he avoids a long chain of trouble. This fits the theme of stopping a quarrel before it starts.

phrases.english: There was a certain man who was saying as he walked
Fortunate is one who hears and stays silent
a hundred troubles pass him by

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first story signaled by the memory aid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Staying silent when insulted spares a person a hundred troubles.

steps.title: שמואל finds the saying in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: שמואל tells רב יהודה that the saying is hinted in 'פוטר מים ראשית מדון', read as 'ריש מאה דיני', the beginning of a hundred disputes.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to רב יהודה: A פסוק says, 'The beginning of strife is like letting out water': the beginning of a hundred disputes.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל shows that the passerby's saying already appears in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל reads 'ראשית מדון' as 'ריש מאה דיני', the start of a hundred disputes. Letting an insult go (פוטר) stops all those fights before they begin. This brings the section back to the same פסוק the סוגיא has been discussing.

keyTerms.meaning: An early אמורא, teacher of רב יהודה
The beginning of a hundred disputes

steps.whatToRemember: The one פסוק 'פוטר מים ראשית מדון' teaches several lessons: about פשרה, about being judged first on Torah, about stopping a fight early, and about staying silent to avoid a hundred fights.

phrases.english: Shmuel said to Rav Yehuda
A verse is written
"The beginning of strife is as when one releases water"
the beginning of a hundred disputes
phrases.notes: שמואל reads ראשית מדון as ריש מאה דיני.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב יְהוּדָה, קְרָא כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק as the source for the passerby's saying in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The popular saying that staying silent saves a hundred troubles.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי 17:14, 'פוטר מים ראשית מדון', read as 'ריש מאה דיני'.

steps.title: A thief is not punished for two or three thefts
steps.stepSummary: A man walking along says that a thief is not killed for only two or three thefts.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man kept saying as he walked: For two or three thefts, the thief is not killed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next folk saying in the series. It sets up שמואל's פסוק, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying means a thief gets a few chances before punishment comes. He is not destroyed right away for his first few thefts. This matches the 'ושתי' (two) part of the memory aid from step 14.

phrases.english: A certain man who kept saying as he walked:
For two or three thefts, the thief is not killed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next saying in the series announced by the memory aid in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thief is given a few chances; he is not punished for only two or three thefts.

steps.title: שמואל finds the thief saying in עמוס
steps.stepSummary: שמואל shows that the פסוק about 'three sins, and for four I will not turn it back' says the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to רב יהודה: A פסוק is written: 'So says ה׳: For three sins of Israel, and for four, I will not turn it back.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a פסוק that backs up the thief saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק counts three sins and then four. It means ה׳ holds back punishment for the first few sins, and the punishment comes at the fourth. That is just like the thief who is not punished for two or three thefts.

keyTerms.meaning: I will not turn it back (I will not hold back the punishment)

phrases.english: Shmuel said to Rav Yehuda:
A verse is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״כֹּה אָמַר ה׳ עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה פִּשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: "So says the Lord: For three sins of Israel
and for four, I will not turn it back."
phrases.notes: עמוס 2:6

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב יְהוּדָה, קְרָא כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק as the source for the saying in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: The saying that a thief is not punished for two or three thefts.
steps.raayaSupportSource: עמוס 2:6: 'For three sins of Israel, and for four, I will not turn it back.'

steps.title: Seven pits for the peaceful man, one for the evildoer
steps.stepSummary: A man says seven pits are dug for a man of peace, and only one for an evildoer.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man kept saying as he walked: Seven pits for the man of peace, and one for the evildoer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next folk saying. It sets up שמואל's פסוק in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The good person may face many traps, but he gets out of all of them. The wicked person needs only one trap to fall for good. This is the 'שבע' (seven) in the memory aid.

keyTerms.meaning: a man of peace, an upright person

phrases.english: A certain man who kept saying as he walked:
Seven pits for the man of peace,
phrases.notes: The idea is that he climbs out of all seven.

phrases.english: and one for the evildoer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next saying in the memory-aid series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The upright person survives many dangers, while the wicked person falls in a single one.

steps.title: שמואל finds the seven-pits saying in משלי
steps.stepSummary: שמואל shows that 'a righteous man falls seven times and rises, but the wicked falls at once' carries the same message.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to רב יהודה: A פסוק is written: 'For a righteous man falls seven times and rises, but a wicked man falls at once.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a פסוק that matches the seven-pits saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lines up with the saying almost word for word. Seven falls for the צדיק, and he gets up each time. The רשע falls with just one.

phrases.english: Shmuel said to Rav Yehuda:
A verse is written:
"For a righteous man falls seven times and rises,
but a wicked man falls at once."
phrases.notes: This joins pieces of two פסוקים: משלי 24:16 and משלי 28:18.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב יְהוּדָה, קְרָא כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק as the source for the saying in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: The saying about seven pits for the good man and one for the evildoer.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי 24:16 and 28:18: 'A righteous man falls seven times and rises, but the wicked falls at once.'

steps.title: Losing a fair court case is still a reason to sing
steps.stepSummary: A man says that someone who leaves בית דין after losing his cloak should still sing and go on his way.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man kept saying as he walked: One who leaves בית דין with his cloak taken from him should sing a song and go on his way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next folk saying. It sets up שמואל's פסוק in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the person who lost the case and had to pay can be happy, because a true judgment was done. Losing what wasn't really his is not a real loss. This is the 'זמירות' (songs) in the memory aid.

phrases.english: A certain man who kept saying as he walked:
One who goes from the court
with his cloak taken from him,
let him sing a song and go on his way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next saying in the memory-aid series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who loses a fair case in בית דין can still leave happy.

steps.title: שמואל finds the court saying in יתרו's advice
steps.stepSummary: שמואל shows that 'all this people shall go to its place in peace' says the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to רב יהודה: A פסוק is written: 'And also all this people shall go to its place in peace.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a פסוק that backs up the court saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'all this people' will go home in peace when there is proper judgment. 'All' includes the side that lost. So when justice is done, even the loser leaves in peace.

phrases.english: Shmuel said to Rav Yehuda:
A verse is written:
"And also all this people
shall go to its place in peace."
phrases.notes: שמות 18:23, from יתרו's advice to משה about setting up judges.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב יְהוּדָה, קְרָא כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק as the source for the saying in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: The saying that one who loses in court should still sing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 18:23: 'All this people shall go to its place in peace.'

steps.title: She dozes and the basket falls
steps.stepSummary: A man says that when she dozes off, the basket falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man kept saying as he walked: She dozes, and the basket falls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the last folk saying hinted at by the memory aid. It sets up שמואל's פסוק in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture a woman carrying a basket on her head. The moment she stops paying attention, the basket drops. The lesson is that carelessness and laziness bring things down. This is the 'הוא' (she) in the memory aid.

phrases.english: A certain man who kept saying as he walked:
She dozes, and the basket falls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final saying in the memory-aid series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carelessness and dozing off cause things to fall apart.

steps.title: שמואל finds the basket saying in קהלת
steps.stepSummary: שמואל shows that 'through laziness the rafters sink' carries the same message, closing the series.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to רב יהודה: A פסוק is written: 'Through laziness the rafters sink,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a פסוק matching the basket saying. This finishes the sayings hinted at by the memory aid, but two more sayings in the same pattern follow in steps 25–29.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says that when people are lazy, the roof beams sag and the house leaks. That is the same idea as the dozing woman whose basket falls. Not paying attention makes things collapse.
steps.whatToRemember: In this series, each folk saying gets a matching פסוק. The usual pattern is 'הָהוּא דַּהֲוָה קָאָמַר וְאָזֵיל' (a man's saying), then 'אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב יְהוּדָה, קְרָא כְּתִיב' (the פסוק behind it). The memory aid 'שמעי ושתי שבע זמירות הוא' lists the first five sayings in order.

phrases.english: Shmuel said to Rav Yehuda:
A verse is written:
"Through laziness the rafters sink," and so on.
phrases.notes: קהלת 10:18

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב יְהוּדָה, קְרָא כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק as the source for the saying in step 23 and closes the sayings listed in the memory aid.
steps.raayaObject: The saying that when she dozes, the basket falls.

steps.title: A saying about a trusted friend who turned against him
steps.stepSummary: A man used to say as he walked that the person he relied on had raised his fist against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who would say as he went along: The man I trusted has lifted his fist and stood against me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another popular saying, this time about being betrayed by someone you trusted. It is setting up the next step, where שמואל will find a פסוק that says the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the earlier sayings: first a folk saying, then a פסוק with the same message. The point here is betrayal by a close friend, which hurts more because you had relied on him.

phrases.english: There was a certain man who would say as he walked along:
The man whom I relied upon
has lifted his fist and stood against me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of folk sayings from steps 21 and 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A popular saying: the friend I trusted turned his fist against me.

steps.title: שמואל finds the same idea in תהלים
steps.stepSummary: שמואל tells רב יהודה that a פסוק in תהלים carries the same message about a trusted friend who betrays you.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to רב יהודה: There is a פסוק that says this: 'Even my close friend, whom I trusted, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל shows that the man's saying already appears in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks about a friend 'in whom I trusted' who 'lifted his heel' against him. That matches the man's words 'the man I relied upon' who 'lifted his fist.' The idea in the folk saying is already in תנ"ך.

keyTerms.meaning: my close friend, literally 'the man of my peace'

phrases.english: Shmuel said to Rav Yehuda:
A verse is written that says this:

phrases.aramaic: ״גַּם אִישׁ שְׁלוֹמִי אֲשֶׁר בָּטַחְתִּי בוֹ וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: "Even my close friend, in whom I trusted, etc."
phrases.notes: תהלים 41:10. The פסוק ends 'has lifted up his heel against me,' which matches the 'fist' in the saying.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב יְהוּדָה, קְרָא כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a פסוק for the saying in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: The saying that a trusted friend turned against him

steps.title: A saying about love making space feel big or small
steps.stepSummary: A man says that when love was strong, a bed as narrow as a sword was enough, but now that love has faded, even a sixty-cubit bed is too small.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who would say as he walked: When our love was strong, we could sleep on a bed as wide as a sword's blade. Now that our love is not strong, a bed sixty cubits wide is not enough for us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more saying, about a marriage where love has cooled. It is setting up רב הונא, who will match it to פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that closeness depends on love, not on space. With love, even a tiny space is enough. Without love, no amount of space is enough.

phrases.english: There was a certain man who would say as he walked along:
When our love was strong,
we could lie on a bed as wide as a sword.
Now that our love is not strong,
a bed sixty cubits wide
is not enough for us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another folk saying in the same series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With love, a tiny space is enough; without love, even a huge space is too small.

steps.title: At first, the שכינה rested in a space ten טפחים high
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says פסוקים express this idea. At first ה׳ spoke from above the כפורת, and the ארון with its כפורת was only ten טפחים high.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: There are פסוקים that say this. At first it is written: 'I will meet with you there and speak with you from above the כפורת.' And a ברייתא teaches: the ארון was nine טפחים high and the כפורת one טפח, which makes ten.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא begins matching the saying to ה׳ and ישראל. This is the first half: when the love was strong, a small space was enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ה׳ spoke 'from above the כפורת.' The ברייתא tells us the ארון and כפורת together were only ten טפחים high. So in the early days of closeness, the שכינה rested in a very small space, like the narrow bed in the saying.

keyTerms.meaning: there are פסוקים written (that say this)
the cover on top of the ארון

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: There are verses written that say this.
At first it is written:
"I will meet with you there
and I will speak with you from above the Ark Cover,"
phrases.notes: שמות 25:22

phrases.english: And a baraita teaches: The Ark was nine handbreadths high,
and the Ark Cover was one handbreadth,
so here there are ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the פסוק-based match for the saying in step 27.
steps.raayaObject: The first half of the saying: with love, a small space is enough
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 25:22 together with the ברייתא about the height of the ארון and כפורת

steps.title: In the end, even the whole world was not enough
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא continues: the בית המקדש was sixty אמה long, and at the end ה׳ says heaven and earth are His throne and footstool, so what house could you build for Me?
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'The house that King שלמה built for ה׳ was sixty אמה long, twenty wide, and thirty high.' And at the end it is written: 'So says ה׳: The heavens are My throne and the earth is My footstool. What house could you build for Me?'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא finishes the match with the second half of the saying: when the love cooled, even a huge space was not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בית המקדש was sixty אמה long, just like the sixty-cubit bed in the saying. Yet at the end, after ישראל sinned, the נביא says no house is enough for ה׳. The story moves from closeness in a ten-טפח space to distance, where even the בית המקדש and the whole world seem too small.

keyTerms.meaning: and at the end, later on

steps.whatToRemember: With love, the שכינה fit in ten טפחים above the ארון. Without it, even the whole בית המקדש, and the world, was 'not enough.' This is exactly the small bed and the sixty-cubit bed of the saying.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״וְהַבַּיִת אֲשֶׁר בָּנָה הַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה לַה׳
phrases.english: And it is written: "And the house that King Solomon built for the Lord,
its length was sixty cubits,
and its width twenty,
and its height thirty cubits."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 6:2

phrases.english: And at the end it is written:
"Thus says the Lord: The heavens are My throne,
and the earth is My footstool;

phrases.aramaic: אֵיזֶה בַיִת אֲשֶׁר תִּבְנוּ לִי וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: what house could you build for Me? etc."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 66:1

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב הונא's match begun in step 28 and ends the series of sayings.
steps.raayaObject: The second half of the saying: without love, even a huge space is not enough

steps.title: How do we know 'לא תגורו' means gathering in?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the earlier teaching on 'לא תגורו' and asks how we know the word means 'gathering in.'
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we see that this word 'לא תגורו' is a word for gathering in?
steps.whatsHappening: The sayings are over, and the גמרא returns to its earlier topic. It asks for proof that 'תגורו' can mean 'gather in.' The next steps will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually 'לא תגורו' is read as 'do not be afraid.' The earlier teaching read it as 'do not hold in (gather in) your words,' meaning a judge must not keep his ruling to himself. So the גמרא wants a פסוק showing the root means 'gathering.'

keyTerms.meaning: from where is it shown? what tells us?
usually 'do not be afraid'; here read as 'do not gather in'

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about fear. The גמרא is reading 'תגורו' with a second meaning, 'gathering in,' and wants proof that the word can mean that.

phrases.english: From where may it be inferred
that this expression "You shall not be afraid [taguru]"
phrases.notes: דברים 1:17

phrases.english: is a term for gathering in?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי לֹא תָגוּרוּ לִישָּׁנָא דְּכַנּוֹשֵׁי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the series of sayings and returns to the earlier reading of 'לא תגורו.'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the root of 'תגורו' means 'gathering in.'

steps.title: רב נחמן: from 'ולא תאגר' about wine
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן brings the פסוק 'you will not drink the wine and you will not gather it,' where the same root means gathering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The פסוק says, 'You will not drink wine and you will not gather it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the first answer, a פסוק where this root clearly means 'gather.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In 'ולא תאגר,' the word means storing or gathering the wine. Since the same root is used, 'לא תגורו' can also mean 'do not gather in.'

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said: The verse states:
"But you shall neither drink of the wine, nor gather it."
phrases.notes: דברים 28:39

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: דברים 28:39, 'ולא תאגר,' uses the root to mean gathering.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב: from the ant who gathers food
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב brings a different פסוק, about the ant who gathers its food at harvest time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said it comes from here: 'She prepares her bread in the summer and gathers her food at harvest time.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different פסוק with the same root meaning 'gather.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'אגרה' clearly means gathering food to store. It is another proof that the root means 'gathering,' brought from a different place.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov says it is derived from here:
"She prepares her bread in the summer,
and gathers her food in the harvest."
phrases.notes: משלי 6:8. The פסוק is talking about the ant.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source from the one in step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משלי 6:8, 'אגרה בקציר מאכלה,' uses the root to mean gathering.

steps.title: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא: from the wise son who gathers
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא brings a third פסוק: 'A wise son gathers in the summer.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, the son of רב איקא, said it comes from here: 'One who gathers in the summer is a wise son.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא brings yet another פסוק where the root means 'gather.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אגר' here describes collecting the crops in summer. All three answers agree on the meaning and differ only in which פסוק they use.
steps.whatToRemember: All three אמוראים prove the same point: the root of 'תגורו' can mean 'gathering in.' So 'לא תגורו' can be read as 'do not hold back your words,' as the earlier teaching said.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא אָמַר מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Ika, says it is derived from here:
"A wise son gathers in the summer."
phrases.notes: משלי 10:5

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא אָמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third source, alongside steps 31 and 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משלי 10:5, 'אגר בקיץ,' uses the root to mean gathering.

steps.title: A memory aid for the coming teachings about judges
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן, a list of three key words (אמת, ממון, יראה) to help remember the three teachings that follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Truth, money, see: this is a memory aid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next three teachings by giving a short memory aid. Each word is a hook for one statement coming right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמת points to the first teaching, about judging with truth. ממון points to the second, about taking money unjustly. יראה points to the third, about how a judge should 'see' himself.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid or sign; a list of key words to remember a series of teachings
Truth; the hook word for the first teaching
Money; the hook word for the second teaching
He should see or view; the hook word for the third teaching

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a statement or a rule. It is only a list of hook words so you can remember the three teachings that come next.

phrases.english: Truth, money, see: a memory aid.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Setup line for the following מימרות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of 'לא תגורו' and opens a new series of teachings about judges.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three teachings follow, keyed to the words אמת, ממון, and יראה.

steps.title: A truthful judge brings the Divine Presence, a false one drives it away
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני quoting רבי יונתן: a judge who rules with complete truth makes the שכינה rest among Israel, and one who does not causes the שכינה to leave. Each half is backed by a פסוק from תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: Any judge who judges with complete truth makes the שכינה rest among Israel, as it says, 'God stands in the gathering of God; among the judges He judges.' And any judge who does not judge with complete truth causes the שכינה to leave Israel, as it says, 'Because of the robbing of the poor, because of the groaning of the needy, now I will arise, says ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first teaching, the one the word אמת was hinting at. It says a judge's honesty decides whether the שכינה stays with Israel or leaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק shows ה׳ standing in the middle of the judges, so an honest court brings Him close. The second פסוק shows ה׳ 'arising' because the poor are oppressed, which is read as Him getting up and leaving. So a dishonest ruling doesn't only hurt one person, it pushes the שכינה away from the whole nation.

keyTerms.meaning: A ruling that is fully true, true all the way through
Causes the Divine Presence to rest

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first teaching hinted at by the word אמת in the memory aid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judge who rules with complete truth brings the שכינה to rest among Israel. A judge who doesn't causes it to leave.

steps.title: A judge who unjustly moves money loses his own soul
steps.stepSummary: Again רבי שמואל בר נחמני quoting רבי יונתן: a judge who unjustly takes money from one side and gives it to the other will have his soul taken by הקדוש ברוך הוא. The proof is a פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: Any judge who takes from this one and gives to that one unjustly, הקדוש ברוך הוא takes his soul from him, as it says: 'Do not rob the poor because he is poor, and do not crush the needy at the gate. For ה׳ will fight their fight and will rob the soul of those who rob them.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second teaching, the one the word ממון was hinting at. A judge who wrongly moves money between the two sides is punished with his life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק warns against crushing the poor 'at the gate', which was where the court sat, so it is talking about judges. The punishment matches the crime: he 'robbed' money through his ruling, so ה׳ 'robs' his soul.

keyTerms.meaning: Not according to the law; unjustly
At the gate, the place where the court sat

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said
Rabbi Yonatan said:
Any judge who takes from this one
and gives to that one unjustly,

and do not crush the needy at the gate;

and will rob the soul of those who rob them.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second teaching in the series, matching the hook word ממון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judge who unjustly takes money from one side and gives it to the other is punished by ה׳ taking his soul.

steps.title: A judge should picture a sword under him and גיהנם open below
steps.stepSummary: A third teaching from רבי שמואל בר נחמני quoting רבי יונתן: a judge should always see himself as if a sword is resting between his thighs and גיהנם is open right beneath him. The teaching continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: A judge should always see himself as if a sword is placed between his thighs, and גיהנם is open beneath him...
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third teaching, the one the word יראה ('he should see') was hinting at. It tells a judge what mental picture to keep while he judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sword picture means that leaning even a little to one side, meaning showing favor, would hurt him right away. גיהנם open below shows the danger is spiritual too. The point is that a judge must judge with real fear and great care.

keyTerms.meaning: גיהנם, the place of punishment after death

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said
Rabbi Yonatan said:
A judge should always see himself

phrases.aramaic: כְּאִילּוּ חֶרֶב מוּנַּחַת לוֹ בֵּין יַרְכוֹתָיו,
phrases.english: as if a sword is placed between his thighs,
and גיהנם is open beneath him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third teaching in the series, matching the hook word יראה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judge must always see himself as if a sword is between his thighs and גיהנם is open beneath him, so he judges with fear and care.
steps.whatToRemember: All three teachings from רבי יונתן (אמת, ממון, יראה) say the same thing in different ways: judging is extremely serious. It affects whether the שכינה stays with Israel, it can cost the judge his life, and he must judge as if danger is right under him.
